extracted.intended_audience: State and local education agencies (SEAs and LEAs), institutions of higher education, nonprofit and for-profit organizations, and tribal organizations applying for or administering ESSA funds
extracted.subtask_description: A reference guide enumerating allowable uses of ESSA funds and eligible entities for specific grant programs (e.g., Title II professional development, Comprehensive Literacy Development Grants). Intended to guide applicants and administrators on program-specific permitted activities and eligible applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based early childhood literacy initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Training providers and personnel to develop and administer evidence-based early childhood education literacy initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically supports development and administration of literacy initiatives in early childhood settings; emphasizes evidence-based approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality professional development for broad educator roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrying out high-quality professional development opportunities for early childhood educators, teachers, principals, other school leaders, paraprofessionals, specialized instructional support personnel, and instructional leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD is intended for a wide range of educators and support staff; 'high-quality' implies content focused on improving instruction and student outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early grades instruction and progress measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing programs and activities to increase the knowledge base of teachers, principals, or other school leaders on instruction in the early grades and on strategies to measure whether young children are progressing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes strategies and tools to assess early childhood progress and improve instruction in early grades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for principals/school leaders on early childhood transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing programs and activities to increase the ability of principals or other school leaders to support teachers, teacher leaders, early childhood educators, and other professionals to meet the needs of students through age 8, which may include providing joint professional learning and planning activities for school staff and educators in preschool programs that address the transition to elementary school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on leadership capacity for transitions from preschool to elementary and coordinated professional learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction for children with disabilities and English learners
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing programs and activities that increase the ability of teachers to effectively teach children with disabilities, including children with significant cognitive disabilities, and English learners, which may include the use of multi-tier systems of support and positive behavioral intervention and supports, so that such children with disabilities and English learners can meet the challenging State academic standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes inclusive instructional strategies, MTSS frameworks, PBIS, and ensuring access to challenging standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized, evidence-based professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing high-quality, personalized professional development that is evidence-based, to the extent the State (in consultation with LEAs in the State) determines that such evidence is reasonably available, for teachers, instructional leadership teams, principals, or other school leaders, that is focused on improving teaching and student learning and achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States determine availability of evidence; PD should be personalized and targeted to improve instruction and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for experiential learning through observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting efforts to train teachers, principals, or other school leaders to participate in opportunities for experiential learning through observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD may include observation-based experiential learning components to improve practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training to support comprehensive literacy instruction (grades 6-12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training principals, specialized instructional support personnel, school librarians, and other LEA personnel to support, develop, administer, and evaluate high-quality comprehensive literacy instruction initiatives for grades 6 through 12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers administrators and specialized staff involved in secondary literacy initiatives; includes development, administration, and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and instruction for gifted and talented students
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing training to support the identification of students who are gifted and talented, including high-ability students who have not been formally identified for gifted education services, and implementing instructional practices that support the education of such students, such as early entrance to kindergarten; enrichment, acceleration, and curriculum compacting activities; and dual or concurrent enrollment programs in secondary school and postsecondary education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes identification processes and differentiated instructional strategies and program options for gifted learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative PD in American history, civics, and geography
rubrics_metrics.description: Expanding, developing, implementing, evaluating, and disseminating for voluntary use, innovative, evidence-based approaches or professional development programs in American history, civics and government, and geography, which must show potential to improve the quality of student achievement in, and teaching of, these subjects; and demonstrate innovation, scalability, accountability, and a focus on underserved populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs must be evidence-based (where reasonably available) and demonstrate potential for improved achievement, scalability, accountability, and focus on underserved students.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality K–5 literacy professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing high-quality professional development opportunities for teachers, literacy coaches, literacy specialists, English as a second language specialists (as appropriate), principals, other school leaders, specialized instructional support personnel, school librarians, paraprofessionals, and other program staff for K–5 literacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets the full K–5 literacy workforce and program staff; 'high-quality' and, where applicable, evidence-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training to support K–5 literacy initiatives (administrative/specialized staff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training principals, specialized instructional support personnel, and other LEA personnel to support, develop, administer, and evaluate high-quality kindergarten through grade 5 literacy initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on capacity-building among leaders and specialized staff to run effective K–5 literacy programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent, family, and community engagement training
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing high-quality, personalized professional development that is evidence-based… including supporting efforts to train teachers, principals, or other school leaders to effectively engage parents, families, and community partners, and coordinate services between school and community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD should equip educators to engage families and coordinate cross-sector services.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD on policy development with community and leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing PD that supports efforts to train teachers, principals, or other school leaders to develop policy with school, LEA, community, or State leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Builds leadership skills related to policy development and cross-level coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of academic content with CTE and work-based learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing high-quality professional development for teachers, principals, or other school leaders on effective strategies to integrate rigorous academic content, career and technical education, and work-based learning (if appropriate), which may include providing common planning time, to help prepare students for postsecondary education and the workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports alignment of academics and CTE/work-based learning and collaboration time for planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-service training on school conditions for learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrying out in-service training for school personnel in addressing issues related to school conditions for student learning, such as safety, peer interaction, drug and alcohol abuse, and chronic absenteeism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at improving school climate and addressing non-academic barriers to learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEM professional development and instructional leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing and providing professional development and other comprehensive systems of support for teachers, principals, or other school leaders to promote high-quality instruction and instructional leadership in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) subjects, including computer science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes building instructional leadership and supports for high-quality STEM teaching, including CS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statewide implementation/expansion of effective STEM PD
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting the implementation, replication, or expansion of effective science, technology, engineering, and mathematics professional development programs in schools across the State through collaboration with school administrators, principals, and STEM educators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds may support scale-up and replication of proven STEM PD programs via collaboration with school leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on appropriate use of student data and privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting and developing efforts to train teachers on the appropriate use of student data to ensure that individual student privacy is protected and in accordance with State student privacy laws and LEA student privacy and technology use policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes legal/compliance aspects of data use and local/state privacy policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training to integrate technology and blended learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting efforts to train teachers, principals, or other school leaders to effectively integrate technology into curricula and instruction, which may include training to assist teachers in implementing blended learning projects (including education about the harms of copyright piracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers digital pedagogy, blended learning implementation, and copyright/piracy education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training to refer students affected by trauma
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrying out in-service training for school personnel in the techniques and supports needed to help educators understand when and how to refer students affected by trauma, and children with, or at risk of, mental illness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on recognition of trauma/mental health issues and appropriate referral actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on referral mechanisms linking to treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrying out in-service training for school personnel in the use of referral mechanisms that effectively link students affected by trauma, and children with, or at risk of, mental illness to appropriate treatment and intervention services in the school and in the community, where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes practical use of referral systems connecting school and community services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training to form partnerships with mental health organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrying out in-service training for school personnel in forming partnerships between school-based mental health programs and public or private mental health organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports developing formal partnerships to expand mental health supports for students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reforming principal/school leader certification and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reforming principal, or other school leader certification, recertification, licensing, or tenure systems or preparation program standards and approval processes to ensure that principals or other school leaders have the instructional leadership skills to help teachers teach and to help students meet such challenging State academic standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds may be used to align leader credentialing and preparation with instructional leadership expectations tied to State standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reforming teacher certification and preparation systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Reforming teacher certification, recertification, licensing, or tenure systems or preparation program standards and approval processes to ensure that teachers have the necessary subject-matter knowledge and teaching skills, as demonstrated through measures determined by the State, which may include teacher performance assessments, in the academic subjects that the teachers teach to help students meet challenging State academic standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on alignment of teacher credentials and assessments with subject-matter and instructional expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aligning teacher certification/licensing with State standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reforming teacher certification, recertification, licensing, or tenure systems or preparation program standards and approval processes to ensure that teacher certification or licensing requirements are aligned with such challenging State academic standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes policy alignment between licensure requirements and State academic goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment of qualified individuals from other fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruiting qualified individuals from other fields to become teachers, principals, or other school leaders, including mid-career professionals from other occupations, former military personnel, and recent graduates of institutions of higher education with records of academic distinction who demonstrate potential to become effective teachers, principals, or other school leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports alternative recruitment pipelines and career changers into education roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training leaders/coaches/mentors/evaluators on performance differentiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing and providing training for school leaders, coaches, mentors, and evaluators on how accurately to differentiate performance, provide useful feedback, and use evaluation results to inform decisionmaking about professional development, improvement strategies, and personnel decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to improve evaluation quality, feedback processes, and data-informed personnel/PD decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD to develop students' learning readiness and essential skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing high-quality, personalized professional development that is evidence-based… including supporting efforts to train teachers, principals, or other school leaders to help all students develop the skills essential for learning readiness and academic success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets interventions and PD that build foundational skills for academic success across student populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible entities: high-need LEAs and early childhood programs (partnerships permitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more LEAs that serve a high percentage of high-need schools; one or more early childhood education programs serving low-income or otherwise disadvantaged children; or any one of these in partnership with one or more public or private nonprofit organizations or agencies that have a demonstrated record of effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies prioritized eligibility for certain grant programs, particularly Comprehensive Literacy and Supporting Effective Instruction-related grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible entities: LEAs, contractors, partnerships with IHEs/tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAs; for-profit or nonprofit entities through a grant or contract from an LEA; or an LEA in partnership with an institution of higher education (IHE), Indian tribe, or tribal organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that non-LEA organizations may participate through grants/contracts or partnerships; common across many listed programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible entities: SEAs for certain activities
rubrics_metrics.description: State educational agencies (SEAs) are listed as eligible entities for specified activities and programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some activities and grant programs specifically permit or target SEAs as applicants or implementers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program and statutory alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses of funds and eligible entities are tied to specific grant programs and statutory citations (e.g., Supporting Effective Instruction State Grants — Title II, Part A; Comprehensive Literacy Development Grants — Title II, Part B, Subpart 2; American History and Civics Education — Title II, Part B, Subpart 3; STEM Master Teacher Corps — Title II, Part B, Subpart 4, section 2245).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should map proposed activities to the correct grant program and statutory authority when seeking ESSA funds.
